questions.q: What is the circuit for measuring the Z1Z2 stabilizer using an ancilla qubit?
options: Swap qubits 1 and 2 and check if the swap changed anything observable
Apply a Hadamard to qubits 1 and 2, then measure both directly
Prepare the ancilla in |0>, CNOT from qubit 1 to the ancilla, CNOT from qubit 2 to the ancilla, then measure the ancilla in the Z basis
Directly measure qubits 1 and 2 in the Z basis and multiply the results
questions.explain: The standard syndrome-extraction circuit uses an ancilla entangled via two CNOTs to the two data qubits being compared, then reads off the ancilla's measurement as the syndrome bit.

questions.q: Why does measuring the ancilla in this circuit reveal whether qubits 1 and 2 agree, but not the encoded data itself?
options: The data qubits are physically disconnected from the ancilla during measurement
Z1Z2 has the same +1 eigenvalue on both logical basis states, so the measurement can only detect a disagreement caused by an error, never distinguish which logical state (or superposition) is encoded
The ancilla measurement always returns 0, regardless of what happens to the data qubits
The CNOT gates used in the circuit have no effect on the ancilla at all
questions.explain: Because both |000> and |111> give the same (+1) Z1Z2 eigenvalue, the measurement can't tell which logical state is present -- it can only detect the error-induced disagreement, which is exactly what makes it non-destructive.

questions.q: Why does this syndrome-extraction mechanism not violate the no-cloning theorem from chapter 2?
options: Nothing about the amplitudes alpha or beta is ever copied or revealed -- only a fact about agreement/disagreement among the physical qubits is extracted
This circuit only works if alpha and beta are both real numbers
The ancilla secretly stores a full copy of the logical qubit's state
No-cloning only applies to classical bits, not to syndrome measurements
questions.explain: The circuit extracts one classical bit of error information (agreement or not) while leaving the superposition over alpha and beta completely undisturbed, which is exactly why it respects no-cloning.

questions.q: How does this ancilla-CNOT-measure pattern relate to more advanced codes like the surface code, covered later in the course?
options: This pattern only works for 2-qubit stabilizers and cannot be extended further
Surface codes measure syndromes by directly reading out the data qubits, unlike this circuit
It is the same underlying circuit primitive, just repeated with more stabilizers, more ancillas, and different wiring across a 2D grid
The surface code uses a completely unrelated mechanism with no ancilla qubits at all
questions.explain: Every stabilizer code in this course, including the surface code, uses the same ancilla-based entangle-then-measure primitive -- just scaled up to more stabilizers measured in parallel.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say real fault-tolerant protocols repeat syndrome extraction multiple times rather than trusting a single round?
options: Syndrome extraction can only be performed once per physical qubit in its lifetime
Repeating syndrome extraction is purely a formality with no practical benefit
The ancilla preparation, CNOTs, and measurement are themselves imperfect physical operations, so a faulty syndrome round could report an incorrect error that isn't actually there
A single round of syndrome extraction always destroys the encoded logical state
questions.explain: Because syndrome-extraction circuits are themselves subject to gate errors and decoherence (chapter 1), repeating rounds and checking consistency helps distinguish a real data error from a faulty measurement round -- a theme developed further in chapter 7.
